epic.name: Sign-in and app shell
unverifiedAssumptions: Verify the sign-in actually sticks: the app assumes the back-end's sign-in cookie survives the trip through the app's own address (the proxy) on localhost. If the cookie is dropped or rejected on the way back, sign-in will appear to succeed but you'll be bounced straight back to the sign-in screen.

Verify you get signed out without clicking: the app assumes the live connection's 'session ended' notice gets through the app's proxy promptly. If the proxy holds the stream back, the first browser in the 'sign in elsewhere' test won't return to sign-in on its own, and only will on your next click.

Verify the 'can't reach the app' message: the app assumes that a stopped back-end produces a recognisable failure through the proxy. If the proxy turns it into something that looks like an ordinary error, you might see a generic error or the wrong message instead of the connection-problem message.

When the back-end is down and you open a signed-in page (e.g. /upload), you are sent to the sign-in screen rather than an error page; the 'can't reach the app' message appears when you then try to sign in. Is that acceptable?
Connection message wording: "We can't reach the app right now. Check your connection and try again." Confirm or reword.

The proxy forwards only the Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, Cookie and Last-Event-ID headers to the back-end (no Origin or Referer). Sign-in works this way; confirm no later endpoint depends on other headers.
The no-access screen shows the heading 'No access' above the approved message. Is that heading wording acceptable?
Success messages close themselves after 5 seconds. Is that the right length of time?
Warning messages (none are raised yet) are announced immediately but still close after 5 seconds; only Problem messages stay on screen. Is that what you want?
The sign-in 'can't reach the app' message stays inside the sign-in card (persistent, announced to screen readers) rather than as a pop-up message. Acceptable?

Wording check: idle timeout says "You were inactive for 60 minutes, so we signed you out. Sign in again to continue."; sign-in elsewhere says "Your account was signed in on another device or browser, so we signed you out here." Acceptable?
When signed out by signing out on another device, this tab returns to the plain sign-in screen with no explanation. Confirm no "you signed out elsewhere" message is wanted.
When three problem messages are already showing and a success message arrives, four messages show briefly instead of three. Check this looks acceptable on a narrow screen.

manualTestResults.by: Claude (automated browser walkthrough against the real back-end, per user preference)
manualTestResults.notes: All checklist items and all check-these-first items passed against the real back-end on :5100 via the production build on :3200. Sign-in-elsewhere returned the first browser to sign-in in ~15s without a click. Back-after-sign-out verified with a 3-page history.
